statement: A claim that cannot be proved until its head is published has a lifecycle instead of a dead end. Landing required a green doneWhen and landing produced the head, so a quest whose evidence is hosted runs on a published tree could never close; its own parent recorded that the more rigorous sealing was the one the machinery punished. A quest may now declare that its claim needs a published head, and optionally what proving its implementation means. Landing such a quest measures the implementation rather than the claim and leaves it awaiting external proof, a state it carries and never a terminal one; the quest stays open until something measures the sealed claim and records the exact head that proof certifies. The closure may live on a later head, but which tree was actually proven is never left to inference. The case is generic and additive: it is not a mode for one kind of evidence, and a quest that proves its claim locally still closes in one step with nothing about it changed.

constraints.statement: The case is a lifecycle state, not a special path for hosted CI. Nothing in it names a workflow, a runner or a provider, and any claim whose evidence needs a published head uses it.
A quest that proves its claim locally is unchanged: it lands and closes in one step. The new state is reachable only by a quest that declares its claim needs a published head.
Closure records the exact implementation head the external proof certifies. A closure that cannot say which tree was proven is refused.
